## Context

Agents sometimes botch the `rebar-ticket:` trailer, leaving a ticket's change unlinkable at close time. The `COMMITS` event type and `attach_commits` reducer already exist (used by the code-review workflow) — what is missing is an author-facing repair surface and a consumer. Approved design (analysis ticket b902-18af-14ed-4da1): expose retroactive commit linking on ALL THREE surfaces (CLI, Python library, MCP), document it clearly, and then add a cheap deterministic close-gate check that the linked change's diff is consistent with the recorded file_impact. Explicitly OUT of scope: using the linked commits as a completion-verifier diff basis — linked commits may be incomplete even when they match file_impact, and CV already prefetches from file_impact.

## Plan

1. CLI verb `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the existing `rebar.attach_commits` seam (validate each SHA resolves in the repo; union-add semantics unchanged).
2. Library re-export (`rebar.attach_commits` already importable — confirm and document) and MCP tool (`attach_commits`) with outputSchema, following the existing write-tool pattern.
3. DET close check. Commit-set discovery is exactly the two sources that already exist, unioned: (i) `state.commits` populated by COMMITS events (the attach-commits surface added here), and (ii) the referencing-commit scan the close gate's completion precheck already performs (commits reachable from the worktree HEAD carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject for the ticket or a descendant). For each discovered commit, collect `git show --name-only` changed paths; a changed path that is neither within the recorded `file_impact` nor matched by this feature's OWN exemption globs (`tests/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — defined and documented here, not inherited from any other gate) is a deterministic close BLOCK naming the offending commit and paths. No LLM. A ticket with no discovered commits keeps today's behavior (the existing cannot-confirm-work-landed error), and a ticket without `file_impact` is out of scope for this check.
4. Documentation: `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/mcp-reference.md`, and the commit-trailer guide (`rebar explain commit-trailer` source) each name the repair verb and when to use it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>` records a COMMITS event and `rebar show` reflects it; invalid SHAs are rejected with a clear error. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -k "attach_commits" -x` passes.
- [ ] The MCP server exposes `attach_commits` with an outputSchema and the Python library documents the call; both route through the same seam as the CLI. Verify: MCP tool-inventory test updated and passing.
- [ ] With file_impact recorded and linked commits present, a commit touching a path outside the declared impact deterministically blocks close with the offending paths named; a conforming diff does not block. Verify: unit tests cover both directions.
- [ ] The three docs name the verb and the repair workflow. Verify: grep assertions in the docs test tier.
